chunks.text: Visitors to local business websites arrive with specific, narrow questions — typically hours, location, menu/services, and contact — and abandon quickly if the answer is not immediately visible.

Hours and location are consistently the highest-priority information across studies, yet are frequently relegated to the footer or a separate "Contact" page that first-time visitors rarely click through to.
First-time visitors rarely scroll below the fold on a local business homepage when they have a specific question; they scan the first screen and leave if the answer is not there.
Mobile visitors are under more time pressure than desktop visitors (they are often in transit, hungry, or making an immediate plan) and abandon even faster when friction appears.
The fix is structural: surface critical information in the hero or a sticky header, repeat it in the footer for reassurance, and ensure mobile layouts do not push it below a scroll.

Why your restaurant loses reservations every night Leak number 3 — "hours are hiding" — is built on NNGroup's finding that hours are the most-searched-for and most-hidden piece of information on restaurant sites.

How much does a custom restaurant website cost in twenty twenty-six? The "what a custom site actually delivers" section leans on this research to explain why hero-placement of hours and location is treated as a baseline, not a premium feature.
Nielsen, J., & Pernice, K. Usability of Local Business Websites . Nielsen Norman Group. nngroup.com
